title: Crest-line feature detection (Yoshizawa-style ridge/valley tracing)
description:
Replace/augment the current magnitude-threshold principal-curvature features with traced crest lines. Current feature detection misses three failure modes observed on voyage_skull_ref.obj:

- Nose-hole (piriform aperture) rim: patches wrap across the ≥90° crease because individual edge dihedrals along the rim dip below T_FEATURE_RAD and the per-vertex magnitude threshold does not capture locally-prominent ridges.
- Orbital rim and zygomatic arch: smooth mesh but perceptually sharp ridge lines; current code has no notion of ridge continuity, so a single sub-threshold vertex breaks the feature set and region growing walks through.
- Inter-tooth gaps: detected but then swallowed by the small-component merge because tooth patches fall below MIN_PATCH_FACES.

Research anchor: Ohtake 2004 / Yoshizawa 2005 'Fast and Robust Detection of Crest Lines on Meshes'. CGAL's Ridges_3 package is the reference production implementation.

Approach: pure Java Yoshizawa-lite.

1. PrincipalDirectionField (new class) — per-vertex shape-operator eigendecomposition in the tangent plane. Output: (κ_max, dir_max, κ_min, dir_min) per vertex. Reuses face-normal averaging and Meyer-style estimators already in SemanticPatchDecomposer.

2. CrestLineDetector (new class) — takes ArrayMesh + PrincipalDirectionField, emits Set<Long> of mesh edges that crest polylines cross.
   a. Candidate selection: |κ_max(v)| > T_RIDGE_SCALE · median(|κ_max|) — adaptive threshold.
   b. Non-maximum suppression along dir_max: keep v as ridge point only if |κ_max(v)| is max among 1-ring neighbours along the eigenvector direction.
   c. MVS threshold (Moreton-Sequin): reject near-umbilical points where (κ_max − κ_min)² is small.
   d. Polyline tracing: walk along dir_max, snap to nearest ridge-point neighbour at each step.
   e. Edge intersection: each polyline segment marks the two face edges it crosses.

3. Adaptive T_FEATURE_RAD — p85 of per-mesh dihedral distribution, not hard-coded 0.20 rad.

4. Union crest edges + principal-magnitude edges + adaptive dihedral edges into the feature-edge set consumed by featureCutAdjacency; region growing / merge / quality split are unchanged.

5. Debug CLI: PatchDecomposerCLI crest-lines <obj> <out_obj> emits the detected polylines as an OBJ with line primitives for Blender visual inspection.

Depends on: nothing. Builds on existing PATCH-6/7/8 scaffolding.
Blocks: PATCH-3 (recursive subdivision), PATCH-9 (DSL scaffold generator) — both depend on correct patch boundaries.
definition-of-done: CrestLineDetector + PrincipalDirectionField classes ship. Adaptive dihedral threshold in place. PatchDecomposerCLI crest-lines subcommand emits an OBJ that visually matches the salient ridges of a skull (nose rim, orbital rim, zygomatic, tooth gaps). Viewer patch overlay on voyage_skull_ref.obj shows individual teeth as distinct patches and patch boundaries that hug socket/aperture rims. breasts.obj patch count stays within a factor of 2 of the pre-PATCH-11 baseline (~1351).
testing-plan: (1) Build and run crest-lines CLI on voyage_skull_ref.obj \u2192 /tmp/crest.obj; open alongside skull in Blender; verify rims + teeth coverage. (2) Launch mesh-viewer, load skull OBJ, P then Shift+P, zoom dentition to confirm individual teeth. (3) uv run label-patches on the skull, confirm anatomical labels reflect proper boundaries. (4) Regression on breasts.obj: patch count order-of-magnitude match, cleaner visible boundaries.
